notes: STALE DESCRIPTION CONFIRMED SHARED: the `name` field's own description on THIS capability still reads verbatim: 'Must be wrapped in a `folder` object — the handler reads a required `folder` wrapper, so a flat body is a 400 before any field is looked at.' That is the exact same false sentence flagged on create_root_folder_v1's `name` field, word for word. It directly contradicts this capability's own top-level `guidance` ('Send the fields flat. The `folder` wrapper is added for you from each field's json_path, and sending your own `folder` object is rejected before the call as an unknown body key.'), and the live call proves guidance right and the field description wrong: a flat body succeeded on attempt 1, no wrapper, no retry needed. This is not a one-off — it is the same template defect present on at least two folder-family capabilities (create_root_folder_v1, create_sub_folder_v1), which means every other create/rename endpoint sharing this parameter template should be assumed stale until checked, not treated as independent bugs. FIVE UNDECLARED-FOLDER-FIELDS CHECK (per instructions): of the five fields flagged as undeclared on create_root_folder_v1's data.folder (root, notes, created_by, updated_by, attachments), FOUR reproduce identically here — root, created_by, updated_by, attachments are all present in the actual response and absent from the 200 schema's folder properties. The fifth, `notes`, could not be checked the same way: this probe did not send a `notes` value, and the response has no `notes` key at all (unlike root-folder's response, which always echoes notes because the probe there explicitly sent one). So `notes` is UNVERIFIED here, not confirmed absent-when-declared — it simply was not exercised. In its place, this capability returns a NEW undeclared field root-folder's list doesn't have to fill the fifth slot in the same structural way: `parent_id`. That one carries an extra wrinkle: describeCapability's own contract is internally split on it — the flat top-level `returns` array lists both `notes` and `parent_id` as returned keys, but the nested 200 JSON schema's `data.folder.properties` lists neither. The actual response includes `parent_id` (undeclared-per-schema, declared-per-returns-list) and omits `notes` (declared-per-returns-list, absent-in-practice, unsent-in-this-probe). That disagreement between describeCapability's two own declaration surfaces (summary `returns` list vs. structured `schema`) is itself worth flagging to whoever maintains the index — they are not reporting the same contract. PROJECT SERIALIZER QUESTION (per instructions): does not apply here — this capability returns no `data.project` object at all, exactly as its own guidance says. So it cannot be matched against either of the two known project serializers (the leaky one from create_root_folder_v1 or the clean one from create_project_v1); the leaky-serializer defect is confirmed specific to root-folder creation, not a folder-family-wide response shape. ID TYPE CHECK (per instructions): `id` (765817) and `parent_id` (765811) are both plain JSON integers in this response, not quoted strings — the id-as-quoted-string inconsistency flagged elsewhere in the family does NOT reproduce on this capability. ENTITLEMENT GATE: not applicable — this call returned an ordinary 200 with `success:true`, no `{success:false}` refusal-wearing-200 pattern observed. ERROR ENVELOPE: not exercised — the single attempt succeeded, so per instructions no error body was diffed against the success schema.
